findings.F1: Fees remove the whole gain: the book earns 1.30e-5 per bar before fees but pays 2.10e-5 per bar in fees, so the 10,709 trades (all long) average +0.083% before fees and -0.017% after, about 0.10% of cost per round trip.
findings.F2: The loss is the same in every period, not one bad stretch: the book's mean daily return is negative in 16 of 24 windows (for example w3 -0.00143, w1 -0.00072), including windows where holding the coin gained (w4 coin +0.0028, book -0.00043; w21 coin +0.0057, book -0.00016).
findings.F3: The two-hour forward move the book trades is about the size of one round-trip fee: on 20:00 UTC bars with forecast > 0 the excess 2-hour return is +0.0006 to +0.0018 by forecast quintile (t 7.39, n 8,613), against roughly 0.0010 of fees per trade.
findings.F4: The traded forecast is barely graded: its quintiles give excess 2-hour returns of +0.0013, +0.0006, +0.0009, +0.0018 and +0.0013 from smallest to largest forecast, and bars with forecast 0 still give +0.0005.
findings.F5: The raw volatility-scaled 24-hour fall is graded where the standardised forecast is not: among falls, the two deepest quintiles (mean z -1.71 and -0.86) give excess 2-hour returns of +0.0019 and +0.0022, against +0.0003 to +0.0012 for the shallower three.
findings.F6: After the deepest raw falls the rise carries on over a full day and grows past the fee: the excess 24-hour return is +0.0018 and +0.0026 for the two deepest z quintiles, against -0.0001, -0.0010 and -0.0017 for the shallower three (n about 1,630 each).
findings.F7: The second hour of the hold loses money: trades held at most 60 minutes average +0.28% before fees (n 3,926), while trades held 60 to 120 minutes average -0.06% (n 6,451); the hour-22 bars carry 2.2e-4 of fees per bar against a gain of -1.3e-6.

ideas.idea: Each coin rises over the 24 hours after 21:00 UTC, and the larger its fall over the past 24 hours measured in units of its 7-day hourly volatility (the raw scaled fall, not that fall ranked against its own recent values), the larger that rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold the evening rebound for a day instead of two hours, so that a move several times one round-trip cost pays for a single fee, and would size it by the raw volatility-scaled fall.
ideas.name: evening drop day-long rebound

ideas.idea: Each coin rises over the two hours after 21:00 UTC, and the larger its fall over the past 24 hours measured in units of its 7-day hourly volatility, the larger that rise, with the rise concentrated in the first hour after 21:00 UTC.
ideas.consequence: A trader would keep only the first hour of the evening rebound, the hour that carries the gain, and would stop paying for a second hour that loses.
ideas.name: first-hour evening drop bounce
